fields.value: Replication Do-Files for the paper "Anything but hard discount: Storevorousness and the social stratification of grocery shopping venues in Italy (2014–2022)"

dsDescriptionValue.value: This replication package contains the Stata do-files used to produce all results and figures reported in the paper. The analysis draws on the Italian Household Budget Survey (HBS) conducted by ISTAT, covering the years 2014–2022.

publicationCitation.value: Oncini, F. (2026). Anything but hard discount: Storevorousness and the social stratification of grocery shopping venues in Italy, 2014–2022. Journal of Consumer Culture, in press

fields.value:
The package comprises the following do-files:

Dependent_variables_FINAL.do — construction of binary store-visit indicators and aggregate purchase measures across seven venue types
Control_variables_FINAL.do — preparation of sociodemographic and socioeconomic control variables
Descriptives_FINAL.do — summary statistics for all key variables
Descriptives_over_time_FINAL.do and Summary_table_descriptives_over_time_FINAL.do — time-trend descriptives and tabulation (2014–2022)
Histograms_FINAL.do — distribution plots of venue-specific purchase counts
Countfit_for_nbreg_FINAL.do — overdispersion diagnostics to justify negative binomial estimation
Model_1__total__FINAL.do — OLS regression of total store voracity on household characteristics, with marginal means by income decile and education
Model_2__HHI__FINAL.do — zero-one-inflated beta (ZOIB) regression of the Herfindahl–Hirschman Index of shopping concentration
Model_3__logit_and_nbreg__FINAL.do — two-part models (logit + negative binomial) for each of the seven store types, with combined margin plots
Poisson_margins_FINAL.do — alternative Poisson-based margins for robustness
Model_4_Margins_per_food_item_Q5-Q1_FINAL.do — Q5–Q1 margin differences by food product and store type
Heatmap_Google_Colab_Script.txt — link to the Python/Google Colab script used to produce the food-item × store-type heatmap

All do-files are self-documented with inline annotation. File paths in the scripts refer to the authors' local environment and must be updated to match the replicator's directory structure.

value: The microdata can be requested via the ISTAT website. For more information visit: https://www.istat.it/informazioni-sulla-rilevazione/spese/

fields.value: The underlying microdata are not included in this package, as access is restricted to authorised researchers via ISTAT. Information on how to apply for access is available at https://www.istat.it/informazioni-sulla-rilevazione/spese/

files.description: Prepares the sociodemographic and socioeconomic covariates used across all models, including household size, age group, sex, marital status, employment status, self-production, education, equivalised expenditure decile, macro-region, municipality size, absolute poverty status, and car ownership.
files.label: Control variables_FINAL.do

dataFile.description: Prepares the sociodemographic and socioeconomic covariates used across all models, including household size, age group, sex, marital status, employment status, self-production, education, equivalised expenditure decile, macro-region, municipality size, absolute poverty status, and car ownership.

files.description: Runs overdispersion diagnostics by comparing mean and variance of venue-specific purchase counts, and fits competing count models (Poisson, negative binomial, zero-inflated variants) to justify the two-part modelling strategy.
files.label: Countfit for nbreg_FINAL.do

dataFile.description: Runs overdispersion diagnostics by comparing mean and variance of venue-specific purchase counts, and fits competing count models (Poisson, negative binomial, zero-inflated variants) to justify the two-part modelling strategy.

files.description: Constructs the main outcome variables: binary indicators of whether each household purchased groceries at each of seven venue types (traditional store, street market, hard discount, hypermarket, supermarket/grocery, farm/producer outlet, international/ethnic store) and an aggregate count of product–venue purchases used as the storevorousness index.
files.label: Dependent variables_FINAL.do

dataFile.description: Constructs the main outcome variables: binary indicators of whether each household purchased groceries at each of seven venue types (traditional store, street market, hard discount, hypermarket, supermarket/grocery, farm/producer outlet, international/ethnic store) and an aggregate count of product–venue purchases used as the storevorousness index.

files.description: Produces summary statistics (frequencies and means) for all key variables, as well as conditional summaries of purchase counts by venue type among purchasing households.
files.label: Descriptives_FINAL.do

dataFile.description: Produces summary statistics (frequencies and means) for all key variables, as well as conditional summaries of purchase counts by venue type among purchasing households.

files.description: Generates figures illustrating trends in store-type uptake and purchase intensity across the 2014–2022 survey waves, used to contextualise the panel of cross-sections.
files.label: Descriptives over time_FINAL.do

dataFile.description: Generates figures illustrating trends in store-type uptake and purchase intensity across the 2014–2022 survey waves, used to contextualise the panel of cross-sections.

files.description: Generates distribution plots of conditional purchase counts for each venue type (among households that shopped there), used to motivate the choice of negative binomial over Poisson estimation.
files.label: Histograms_FINAL.do

dataFile.description: Generates distribution plots of conditional purchase counts for each venue type (among households that shopped there), used to motivate the choice of negative binomial over Poisson estimation.

files.description: Estimates an OLS regression of the aggregate storevorousness index on all covariates with robust standard errors, and computes adjusted predictions (marginal means) by expenditure decile and education level, producing the key stratification figures in the paper.
files.label: Model 1 (total)_FINAL.do

dataFile.description: Estimates an OLS regression of the aggregate storevorousness index on all covariates with robust standard errors, and computes adjusted predictions (marginal means) by expenditure decile and education level, producing the key stratification figures in the paper.

files.description: Estimates a zero-one-inflated beta (ZOIB) regression of the Herfindahl–Hirschman Index of shopping concentration, modelling simultaneously the probability of exclusive reliance on a single venue type, the probability of maximally dispersed shopping, and the continuous concentration score in between.
files.label: Model 2 (HHI)_FINAL.do

dataFile.description: Estimates a zero-one-inflated beta (ZOIB) regression of the Herfindahl–Hirschman Index of shopping concentration, modelling simultaneously the probability of exclusive reliance on a single venue type, the probability of maximally dispersed shopping, and the continuous concentration score in between.

files.description: Runs venue-specific two-part models: a logit for the probability of visiting each store type and a negative binomial for purchase frequency conditional on visiting, then computes and combines income-gradient margin plots across all seven venues.
files.label: Model 3 (logit and nbreg)_FINAL.do

dataFile.description: Runs venue-specific two-part models: a logit for the probability of visiting each store type and a negative binomial for purchase frequency conditional on visiting, then computes and combines income-gradient margin plots across all seven venues.

files.description: Computes Q5–Q1 marginal differences (top vs. bottom expenditure decile) in purchase probabilities for each combination of food product (20 items) and store type (7 venues), producing the data underlying the heatmap figure.
files.label: Model 4 Margins per food item_Q5-Q1_FINAL.do

dataFile.description: Computes Q5–Q1 marginal differences (top vs. bottom expenditure decile) in purchase probabilities for each combination of food product (20 items) and store type (7 venues), producing the data underlying the heatmap figure.

files.description: Replicates the margin plots from Model 3 using Poisson rather than negative binomial regression, serving as a robustness check for the conditional frequency estimates.
files.label: Poisson margins_FINAL.do

dataFile.description: Replicates the margin plots from Model 3 using Poisson rather than negative binomial regression, serving as a robustness check for the conditional frequency estimates.

files.description: Produces a structured summary table of annual shares and averages by store type and year, used as a reference for the descriptive section of the paper.
files.label: Summary table descriptives over time_FINAL.do

dataFile.description: Produces a structured summary table of annual shares and averages by store type and year, used as a reference for the descriptive section of the paper.
